text:
sarah_support: FYI — ACME is hitting repeated 504s from the hosted inference gateway during a large embeddings run around 12:13 UTC. They see streaming timeouts and the client sees 504s from the edge. Attached sample request/response and trace ids they shared.

sarah_support: sample curl they ran:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'X-Request-ID: rr-1234' --http2 https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -d '{"input": ["...large batch..."]}'
```

sarah_support: response snippet:
```
< HTTP/2 504 
< server: envoy
< x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 30002
< x-redwood-trace: trace-7f9c
```

mike_oncall: Thanks — grabbing the trace now. Can you paste the trace ids and a few request_ids? I want the x-redwood-trace + X-Request-ID. Also how long did the client wait before timeout?

sarah_support: They included trace-7f9c, rr-1234, rr-1259. Client timeout ~= 30s. They said this started ~5m after a deploy that changed auth cache TTL from 10m -> 1m (canary).

mike_oncall: Noted. Envoy 504 + upstream_service_time ~= 30s. That smells like upstreams either stuck or upstream connection pool drained and requests queued until timeout. I'll pull envoy /stats and connection counters.

mike_oncall: quick checks run:
```
curl -s localhost:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx_active
curl -s localhost:9901/stats | grep upstream_rq_pending_active
ss -ntp | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
```

mike_oncall: On the host serving that trace: upstream_rq_pending_active spiked to ~120, upstream_cx_active near limits, and we have many TIME_WAIT sockets on upstream auth service.

mike_oncall: hypothesis: the auth cache TTL drop caused a thundering of auth backend calls. Auth backend is slower under load -> upstreams exhausting connection pool -> envoy queues requests -> client timeouts -> 504s.

eva_engsre: I see the same across a few nodes. Additional observations from envoy logs: repeated 502/504 pattern with logs showing "upstream request timeout" and "no healthy upstream" intermittently. Also H2 keepalive pool entries show rapid churn.

eva_engsre: Repro steps we've used locally:
1) set auth cache TTL to 30s on a canary host
2) send many concurrent emb endpoint requests with batch size 64 (50 clients)
3) watch upstream auth QPS and envoy pending request metrics

eva_engsre: Commands to snapshot state for triage:
```
curl -s localhost:9901/stats | egrep 'upstream_rq_pending|upstream_cx_active|cluster\.\S+\.rq_.*'
curl -s localhost:9901/server_info
journalctl -u envoy -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 100
ss -s
```

eva_engsre: Short-term mitigations:
- rollback the auth-cache TTL canary (if still running) -> immediate drop in auth QPS
- increase envoy cluster max connections / connection pool for auth cluster (temporary)
- enable a relaxed circuit for auth backend so we fail fast to a cached path instead of queueing

eva_engsre: Longer-term fixes:
- add jittered cache TTL on auth token refresh to avoid synchronized expiry across nodes
- tune upstream connection pool and per-host concurrency limits for high-batch endpoints (embedding traffic pattern)
- add metric alerting on upstream_rq_pending_active crossing a small threshold for autoscaling/mitigation

deploy-bot: roll forward note: canary for auth-cache-ttl=60s was deployed 12:08 UTC to 10% of hosts (rolling). At 12:13 we saw elevated auth calls on canary hosts. No automatic rollback triggered.

mike_oncall: Action plan now:
- sara_support: message ACME that we're investigating and request a short repro window (5m) and say we may throttle batch size as temporary mitigation.
- eva_engsre: perform immediate canary rollback for auth-cache-ttl change and increase cluster.connections for auth service on the affected gw ASGs.
- I'll collect full envoy admin dumps and forward traces + logs to SRE channel.

sarah_support: Ack. I'll ping ACME and request traces and whether they can try smaller batch size while we work.

mike_oncall: Pushed a rollback to the canary group (ID 2) — monitoring for reduction in pending queues. If that drops, we'll roll back remainder.

eva_engsre: After rollback, pending queue fell ~85% on canary nodes and 504 reports stopped within ~90s. We'll keep the auth TTL at previous value and schedule a staging test with jittered TTL.

sarah_support: I'll update the customer: explain root cause (auth cache TTL reduction causing auth backend storm -> upstream pool exhaustion -> envoy queued requests -> 504s) and note rollback + next steps. Customer success tagged as FYI.

mike_oncall: Leaving this thread open until postmortem note is posted. Add perf graphs from envoy stats and auth QPS to the incident ticket.
